question: Can explicit membrane-potential noise make deep spiking networks trainable as probabilistic models while improving accuracy, perturbation robustness, and neural-response modeling?

key_findings.claim: NSNN turns a noisy leaky integrate-and-fire threshold into a Bernoulli spike probability controlled by the noise CDF.
key_findings.evidence: Adding symmetric zero-mean Gaussian membrane noise yields P(spike)=F_epsilon(u-v_threshold); vanishing variance recovers a deterministic threshold. Layer/time spike states define a directed probabilistic graphical model that can be sampled in ordinary SNN architectures.

key_findings.claim: Noise-driven learning gives surrogate gradients a probabilistic interpretation, but the implemented estimator is biased rather than an exact likelihood gradient.
key_findings.evidence: Local marginalization expresses each binary unit's contribution through the loss difference under a spike flip. To avoid repeated forward evaluations, Equation 17 replaces that difference by a first-order derivative; the paper explicitly notes bias except for multilinear downstream maps. The resulting postsynaptic factor is the membrane-noise density F'_epsilon(u-v_threshold), algebraically matching a surrogate derivative.

key_findings.claim: Across several image and event-camera benchmarks, tuned noisy variants generally outperform matched deterministic SNN families.
key_findings.evidence: Reported combinations of STBP/TET/tdBN with CIFARNet, ResNet, VGG-SNN, and 7B-Net improve clean test accuracy on CIFAR-10/100, DVS-CIFAR, and DVS-Gesture; one CIFAR-10 pair rises from 91.88% to 93.90%. Moderate noise standard deviations around 0.2-0.5 work best, and sampling adds roughly 6% training time in one example.

key_findings.claim: Noise-trained models show higher measured resistance to adversarial, event-drop, and spike-flip perturbations, though robustness evaluation remains limited.
key_findings.evidence: FGSM and constrained direct-optimization attacks on CIFAR and EventDrop/spike-state flips on event data produce higher accuracy/lower loss for NSNNs at most tested intensities; the gap reaches 46.3 percentage points for one severe DVS-CIFAR spike-flip setting. No adaptive expectation-over-randomness attack, certified bound, or equal-clean-accuracy control is reported.

key_findings.claim: The paper's claimed Lyapunov proof that additive noise accelerates self-correction appears internally inconsistent.
key_findings.evidence: The coupled-trajectory analysis drives perturbed and unperturbed states with the same Wiener process. For additive diffusion g=a2*1 (b2=0), Delta g=g(u+epsilon)-g(u)=0, so the noise cancels from error dynamics. Yet Theorem 1 assumes a2||epsilon|| <= ||Delta g|| and later applies it with a2>0,b2->0 to claim a more negative exponent; that assumption cannot hold in the stated additive case.

key_findings.claim: NSNN better captures trial variability in a small retinal-fitting case, but its neuroscience claims exceed the validation scope.
key_findings.evidence: On 49 salamander retinal cells from half of one movie/retina recording, an NSNN trained with spike-train MMD visually and correlationally fits variable responses better than a same-architecture DSNN and is competitive with a CNN using fewer parameters. A negative Fano-factor/prediction-similarity correlation on classification models is interpreted as rate coding, without comparison to biological coding hypotheses or held-out animals/stimuli.

method.core_idea: Treat neuronal membrane noise as the source of both stochastic spike computation and a smooth probability derivative for training deep SNNs.
method.mechanism: Inject independent Gaussian noise into discrete LIF membrane updates, sample spikes from the induced threshold-crossing Bernoulli distribution, express the time-unrolled network as a Bayesian network, locally marginalize each binary spike, and approximate spike-flip loss differences to obtain a one-backward-pass three-factor rule. Train varied SNN backbones and test clean, corrupted, adversarial, and neural-fitting behavior.
assumptions: Independent additive Gaussian membrane noise is an adequate abstraction of biological and hardware variability.
A first-order spike-flip loss approximation is accurate enough despite biased gradients in nonlinear deep networks.
Noise CDF density is the appropriate surrogate shape and its variance can be selected without test leakage.
Stochastic inference is fairly compared with deterministic networks after separate hyperparameter grid searches.
The stochastic stability coupling and diffusion assumptions apply to the actual additive-noise NSNN.

techniques.role: Converts threshold spikes into probability distributions using membrane noise.
Represents spike states and temporal dependencies as a probabilistic graphical model.
Reduces score-function variance by exactly summing over one spike state.
Uses noise density as the postsynaptic surrogate factor in backpropagation.
Finds the accuracy/regularization tradeoff between deterministic and over-random firing.
Fits recorded retinal responses using a postsynaptic-potential kernel.

evaluations.setting: CIFAR-10/100, DVS-CIFAR, and DVS-Gesture with multiple deep SNN architectures, algorithms, and simulation lengths.
evaluations.metric: Mean/SD test accuracy, learning curves, and one training-time comparison.
evaluations.result: NSNN variants generally improve over their deterministic counterparts and remain compatible with STBP, TET, tdBN, and several residual/VGG-like backbones.
evaluations.baseline: Matched deterministic LIF SNNs plus reported literature models.

evaluations.setting: CIFAR FGSM/direct-optimization attacks and DVS-CIFAR EventDrop or hidden spike-state flips over multiple intensities.
evaluations.result: NSNN curves degrade more slowly in the reported attacks/perturbations, with especially large gains under severe internal spike flips.

evaluations.setting: Repeated-trial classification coding analyses and 49-cell salamander-retina natural-movie response fitting.
evaluations.metric: Fano factor versus prediction cosine similarity; predicted-recorded Pearson correlation; raster/rate plots; parameter count.
evaluations.result: Trial-rate variability is negatively correlated with output stability, and NSNN fits response variability better than DSNN while competing with a larger CNN.
evaluations.baseline: Deterministic SNN and conventional CNN neural-response model.

limitations: NDL uses a biased first-order loss-difference approximation; calling it a principled gradient solution or saying it subsumes SGL needs qualification.
The additive-noise Lyapunov corollary violates the theorem's own Delta-g lower-bound assumption under the shared-noise coupling.
Robustness is tested with basic attacks and no expectation-over-transformation/randomness adaptation, certification, attack convergence audit, or matched clean accuracy.
Separate grid searches and selected fixed noise levels obscure whether improvements survive equal tuning budgets and preregistered validation.
Energy/latency claims are not measured on neuromorphic hardware; random sampling increases conventional GPU training cost.
The retinal experiment uses a narrow slice of one salamander dataset and does not test cross-retina, cross-stimulus, or likelihood calibration.
Independent white Gaussian noise omits correlated, colored, state-dependent, synaptic, refractory, and device-specific noise.
failure_modes: Too little noise collapses the density-derived surrogate into an uninformative narrow gradient; too much destroys signal.
Gradient bias compounds through time and depth, leading to an optimizer fixed point unrelated to expected-loss minimization.
A stochastic defense masks gradients, and an adaptive EOT adversary removes the apparent robustness advantage.
Inference variance requires many trials, erasing SNN latency and energy benefits.
Hardware noise distribution or correlation differs from training noise and causes a deployment mismatch.
Rate-code conclusions fail when precise timing carries the task-relevant neural information.
reusable_insights: Derive surrogate shapes from an explicit stochastic neuron model, but report whether the resulting network estimator is unbiased.
Test random-noise robustness with adaptive expectation-over-randomness attacks and equal-clean-accuracy baselines.
Audit stochastic stability proofs under the exact coupling used; common additive noise cancels from trajectory differences.
Separate noise used for regularization during training from stochasticity required at inference with a full accuracy-cost curve.
Validate computational-neuroscience models on held-out subjects and stimuli, not only average spike similarity within one recording.
open_questions: Can an unbiased, low-variance, single-pass gradient estimator scale to deep recurrent stochastic SNNs?
Does NSNN robustness survive EOT-PGD, AutoAttack-style suites, common corruptions, and hardware faults at matched accuracy and compute?
What stability statement is valid for independent-noise, shared-noise, and multiplicative-noise couplings of LIF dynamics?
Can noise variance be learned per neuron/time/layer while preserving calibration and hardware efficiency?
Which biological spike statistics and coding tasks require stochastic dynamics beyond rate variability?

competitive_landscape.title: Surrogate Gradient Learning in Spiking Neural Networks: Bringing the Power of Gradient-Based Optimization to Spiking Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Neftci et al. systematize practical surrogate-gradient training for deterministic SNNs. NDL reinterprets the surrogate derivative as an escape-noise density and adds stochastic inference, but retains a biased chain-rule approximation.

competitive_landscape.title: Adaptive Smoothing Gradient Learning for Spiking Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Adaptive smoothing progressively changes random spike relaxation so an analog prototype evolves toward a target SNN and learns its relaxation degree. NSNN instead keeps stochastic membrane firing as the computational model and ties the gradient shape to its fixed noise distribution.

competitive_landscape.title: Natural Gradient Enables Fast Sampling in Spiking Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Masset et al. design population geometry for fast, biologically motivated sampling from correlated distributions. NSNN targets modular supervised deep-SNN training and robustness rather than accurate probabilistic sampling dynamics.

competitive_landscape.title: Elucidating the Theoretical Underpinnings of Surrogate Gradient Learning in Spiking Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Gygax and Zenke independently connect escape noise and stochastic automatic differentiation to surrogate derivatives while explicitly proving that surrogate gradients generally are not gradients of a surrogate loss. This sharpens and qualifies NDL's claimed theoretical rationale.

competitive_landscape.title: Exact Gradients for Stochastic Spiking Neural Networks Driven by Rough Signals
competitive_landscape.difference: Holberg and Salvi derive pathwise exact gradients for event-SDE SNNs with noisy dynamics and spike times using rough paths. Their method is mathematically heavier but directly addresses the exactness gap in NDL's scalable biased estimator.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors claim a general scalable noisy-SNN framework, a theoretically grounded noise-driven rule subsuming surrogate gradients, improved accuracy/robustness, and better neural-coding models.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Equations 1-19 define stochastic firing and NDL; recognition/perturbation tables and Figures 3-5 supply empirical results; Theorem 1 is offered for stability.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Combining deep modular SNNs, explicit membrane noise, and a density-shaped one-pass learning rule is useful engineering and predates close later theory. However, NDL is biased and the stated additive-noise stability proof is not valid under its assumptions. Empirical gains are promising but require adaptive robustness and broader neural/hardware validation.

reviewer_notes: Read all 36 cached pages; page 32 lacked extractable text after OCR but all main text, methods, tables, proofs, references, and surrounding supplement were available. Primary OpenReview/arXiv/publisher competitors through 2024 were checked on 2026-08-23. I explicitly audited Equations 20-23 and Theorem 1: with common additive diffusion, Delta g is zero, making the later a2>0 lower-bound application inconsistent.
